title: Chapter jump rail: a scrollspy of real links that jumps, lands and announces
intent: Chapter jump rail and scrollspy index
summary: One fixed `<nav aria-label>` of six numbered chapter links whose current one (`aria-current="true"`) is the chapter with its midpoint nearest the viewport centre (none above the first chapter or below the last), measured from cached offsets on every Lenis and native scroll; a 2 px rule under each name fills with `scaleX` from the reading position (done chapters full, the current one at the centre line's share of its height); one marker bar moves by a written `translate3d` on the routine band (`.4 s` expo-out) and cuts when it first appears; any in-page chapter link jumps with `lenis.scrollTo` (`1.2 s`, Lenis on the GSAP ticker, `scroll-margin-top` honoured), marks the destination at the start of the glide and holds it until landing, then focuses the chapter heading (`tabindex=-1`, `preventScroll`), writes the hash and announces `Stage n of 6: title` once in a polite status; a wheel, touch or scrolling key mid-glide cancels the landing; below 900 px the same list sits behind a sticky ticket naming the current chapter (`n of 6` + short title) with its own progress rule, a disclosure (`aria-expanded`) closed by Escape, outside taps, Tab out and a jump; reduced motion jumps instantly and keeps the current link, fills and announcements while the marker cuts; forced colours outline the current link
variants: a fixed rail beside the read, a sticky ticket on phones (this, default)
the rail rotated with `writing-mode: vertical-rl` against the right edge, for a page that cannot spare a column
chapters of very unequal length: mark the chapter containing the centre line instead of the nearest midpoint
on a virtual scroll: map the same list to section indices and jump by seeking the scalar
